paragraphs: Swamiji loved telling two short stories about what it really means to love God.

In the first, a man was going through a hard time. His wife was fed up. She kept pointing out how well other people were doing, listed every one of his failures, and finally asked him bitterly what his God had done for him after all his years of devotion. The man did not argue about blessings or rewards. He simply pointed to the mountain in front of them. What did that mountain ever do for him, he asked, and what had he ever done for it? Yet he loved it, because he was made to love what is beautiful. That, he said, was exactly how he loved God. He was not a shopkeeper doing business in religion.

The second story is about a king who wanted to give a gift to a rishi, a sage. The rishi said no, but the king kept insisting until the sage agreed to come along to the palace. There, the rishi heard the king at his prayers, asking God for more wealth, more power and a longer life. The sage listened quietly, puzzled, and at last rolled up his mat and began to walk out.

The king opened his eyes and called after him. Why was he leaving without his gift? The rishi's reply was short and sharp: "I, ask from a beggar?" A king who was still begging God for more had nothing real to give.
learn: Love that keeps a scorecard is really a deal. Whether it is friendship, family or faith, ask yourself whether you value it for what it gives you or for what it is. And notice that people who are always asking for more are, in a way, still poor.
